The concentration of free calcium ions in a solution of 0.02 M Ca-EDTA complex can be determined from the dissociation equilibrium. The formation constant is \(K_f = 5 \times 10^{10}\), so the dissociation constant is \(K_d = 1/K_f = 2 \times 10^{-11}\).

The dissociation reaction is:
\[ \text{CaY}^{2-} \rightleftharpoons \text{Ca}^{2+} + \text{Y}^{4-} \]

Let \(x = [\text{Ca}^{2+}] = [\text{Y}^{4-}]\) at equilibrium. The complex concentration is \(0.02 - x \approx 0.02\) M. Then:
\[ K_d = \frac{[\text{Ca}^{2+}][\text{Y}^{4-}]}{[\text{CaY}^{2-}]} = \frac{x^2}{0.02} = 2 \times 10^{-11} \]
\[ x^2 = 0.02 \times 2 \times 10^{-11} = 4 \times 10^{-13} \]
\[ x = \sqrt{4 \times 10^{-13}} = 2 \times 10^{-6.5} \approx 6.3 \times 10^{-7} \text{ M} \]

Answer: D
